A hook may BLOCK only when the harm completes at the moment of the action AND lands irreversibly on a THIRD PARTY's artifact, on ANOTHER SESSION's work, or on the MAINTAINER's AWS account (CLAUDE.md, Tooling Policy; roster in .claude/rules/hooks.md). Everything else is a sentence in CLAUDE.md, a unit test over src/**, or nothing. Wired: branch-gate blocks a commit or push whose TARGET tree is on main; stale-base-gate blocks a `git push` whose branch sits on origin/main yet reverts files recent main commits changed (the stale-base soft-reset clobber); ci-green-gate blocks `gh pr merge` unless every GitHub Actions check reports pass or skipping; bughunt-clean-gate blocks `git commit` / `gh pr create` / `gh pr merge` while the COMMITTING owner's bug-hunt sentinel still lists un-deleted AWS resources — per-owner, so a peer session's live hunt does not block an unrelated commit; deploy-autoarm-gate arms that sentinel with a PER-SESSION token the moment a deploy-shaped command runs, so a throwaway live test cannot be forgotten; worktree-guard (matcher Edit|Write|NotebookEdit) blocks a file-tool write into the MAIN checkout's src/** or tests/** while a .worktrees/ worktree exists, because a Write there overwrites whatever uncommitted content another session left in the shared tree and nothing in git holds a copy. env: CLAUDE_CODE_THRIFTY_SONIC is pinned to "0" — Claude Code's bash-first experiment tells a session to write files through cat/sed -i/heredocs instead of Edit/Write, which makes worktree-guard (the only file-tool-matched entry here) stop firing entirely; fenced by tests/bash-first-optout-1893.test.ts.
